conflicts.point: Whether frontier firms achieve exponential output multiplication through agentic AI adoption, proving productivity gains are empirical reality rather than corporate hype.

positions.stance: Frontier firms achieve exponential output multiplication through autonomous agents that replace low-leverage tasks.
Reported gains rely on elite, modular codebases and obscure compounding maintenance liabilities in mixed environments.

conflicts.point: Whether empirical audits of automated pull-request generation show surging merge conflicts and error correction overhead.

positions.stance: Data shows automated code generation increases merge conflicts and error correction work by twenty-four percent within six months.
Throughput gains in high-performing teams dwarf localized debugging interventions.

verdicts.conflict: Whether frontier firms achieve exponential output multiplication through agentic AI adoption or face compounding maintenance liabilities.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position offers more concrete, testable claims regarding error correction overhead and merge conflicts in mixed codebases. The accelerationist claim relies on high-level enterprise case studies that often omit long-term maintenance metrics.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Comprehensive empirical data showing sustained productivity increases across standard corporate codebases over multi-year cycles would tip the balance toward the accelerationists.

verdicts.conflict: Whether empirical audits of automated code generation show surging merge conflicts and error correction overhead.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist argument cites specific error rates and measurable increases in merge conflicts, providing a falsifiable metric. The accelerationist counter-argument dismisses these findings as localized without providing comparable quantitative benchmarks for team-wide throughput.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Peer-reviewed studies proving that team-level velocity metrics consistently outweigh localized debugging time in diverse development teams would reverse this finding.
